title: Forensic Playback Runbook: Residency-Aware Authorization & Audit Evidence
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Summary
This runbook defines the process we use to perform a forensic 'playback' of authorization decisions and audit telemetry for incidents that require compliance-grade evidence packaging. It is designed for incidents that involve cross-region data residency concerns, RBAC anomalies, or suspected exfiltration via model inference endpoints.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-owned hosted and dedicated inference endpoints, and to Private deployments where we provide evidence collection guidance.
- Covers authorization decision reconstruction, audit stream extraction, residency-aware evidence segregation, cryptographic packaging, and handoff to legal/compliance.
- Not a general incident-management guide; use the Incident Triage Flow for broader incident coordination.

Owner and Audience
- Runbook owner: Security Incident & Forensics (security@redwood.com)
- Primary audience: Oncall SRE, Security Engineers, Forensics Engineers, Legal/Compliance SMEs.

Goals and Acceptance Criteria
- Complete reconstruction of the authorization decision chain (who/what/when) for the incident window.
- Audit event capture that preserves context, ordering, and cryptographic integrity.
- Residency-preserving packaging so data subject to sovereignty constraints is isolated and labeled.
- Evidence delivered to Legal/Compliance within SLA: initial package within 4 hours of evidence-ready state; complete package within 72 hours.

Prerequisites
- Access to audit storage (Kinesis/Datastreams / internal audit-bucket) and redwood-audit-cli.
- Decryption keys or access to HSM-stored wrap keys (coordinated with Security Ops).
- Legal/Compliance intake ticket created and an evidence custodian assigned.

Definitions
- Playback window: the time range of interest (start_ts, end_ts).
- Authz chain: the sequence of entitlement checks and policy decisions across services (API gateway, frontend auth, service tokens, model-serving policy).
- Residency label: the geographic/sovereign tag associated with a data shard (e.g., eu, us, apac).

Preparation Checklist (pre-playback)
1) Confirm incident scope and playback window with Incident Commander.
2) Assign Evidence Custodian and Legal reviewer.
3) Note any residency constraints and required redaction policies.
4) Open ephemeral access to audit store (time-limited role) and log all accesses for provenance.

High-Level Playback Procedure
1) Lock the window
   - Freeze automated retention or purge jobs for artifacts within playback window.
   - Mark the window in the audit index so downstream collectors do not rotate/compact relevant shards.
2) Extract authz artifacts
   - Pull authorization logs from the gateway, auth-service, token-issuer, and service-to-service brokers.
   - Command: 
```
redwood-audit-cli extract --streams gateway,auth-service,token-issuer,svc-broker --from 2026-02-09T18:12:00Z --to 2026-02-09T18:45:00Z --out /tmp/playback-20260209
```
   - Verify checksums for each shard: sha256sum *.ndjson > checksums.txt
3) Reconstruct ordering
   - Use event_time + monotonic_sequence to reconstruct causal order across streams.
   - If missing monotonic_sequence, fall back to local-write-timestamp and mark ordering confidence per event.
4) Correlate to model-serving traces
   - Pull request traces (trace-id) and KV-cache hits to determine whether inputs or outputs were cached or replayed.
   - Crosslink trace ids to authz events using the correlation table (column: trace_id -> auth_event_id).
5) Residency-aware segregation
   - Partition extracted artifacts by residency label. Any event touching EU-located data must be stored and packaged separately with EU-only access.
   - Table: Evidence partition rules:
     | Residency | Sources included | Packaging label | Access control |
     |---|---|---|---|
     | eu | gateway logs, auth-service, model-request-logs (eu shard) | EU-EVID-<id> | Legal-EU-only + Security Forensics |
     | us | same as above (us shard) | US-EVID-<id> | Legal-US + Security Forensics |
     | apac | same as above (apac shard) | APAC-EVID-<id> | Legal-APAC + Security Forensics |
6) Complementary artifact capture
   - Grab config snapshots (feature flags, rollout policy, model variant mapping) in effect during window.
   - Example commands: 
```
redwood-configctl snapshot --service modelrouter --at 2026-02-09T18:12:00Z --out /tmp/playback-20260209/configs
kubectl get configmap modelrouter-config -n prod -o yaml > /tmp/playback-20260209/configs/modelrouter-config.yaml
```
7) Evidence proofing and cryptographic binding
   - Compute SHA256 of each artifact and produce a signed manifest using the evidence signing key.
   - Command (example): 
```
cd /tmp/playback-20260209
sha256sum * > sha256sums.txt
redwood-keys sign --key evidence-signing-v2 --in sha256sums.txt --out signed-manifest.sig
```
8) Redaction and minimalization
   - Apply pre-agreed redaction rules for PII before handing to non-EU reviewers. The Evidence Custodian must approve redaction scripts.
   - Maintain an unredacted, encrypted copy in a residency-bound vault; only Legal and Security Forensics may request decryption.
9) Package and handoff
   - Create structured evidence bundle with directory layout: /evidence/<case-id>/<residency>/artifacts, manifest, signed-manifest.sig, checksums.txt, chain-of-custody.md
   - Upload package to evidence-store with time-limited access links and notify Legal via secure channel.

Artifact and Metadata Requirements
- Every artifact must include the following metadata in plain text alongside the file:
  - artifact_id (UUID)
  - source_service
  - original_timestamp
  - extracted_by (engineer id)
  - extraction_timestamp
  - residency_label
  - sha256
  - lineage (upstream artifact ids if derived)

Chain-of-Custody Template (chain-of-custody.md)
1) Collected by: <engineer name> (<email>) on <timestamp>
2) Verified checksums by: <engineer name> on <timestamp>
3) Signed by: Evidence Signing Service (key id) on <timestamp>
4) Transferred to: Legal (name) on <timestamp> via secure upload (link)

Ordering Confidence Tags
- HIGH: monotonic_sequence present across streams and correlation validated.
- MEDIUM: ordering by timestamps with < 1s skew across sources.
- LOW: timestamp-based ordering with > 1s skew or missing correlation.

Playbook: Quick Run (for oncall SRE)
1) Immediately preserve window: `redwood-audit-cli lock --from <start> --to <end>`
2) Run extraction command (see above) and forward checksums to Evidence Custodian.
3) Snapshot runtime configs and model router mapping.
4) Partition artifacts by residency and run signing.
5) Upload to evidence-store and create Legal intake.
Estimated time: 60–180 minutes depending on cross-region scope and dataset size.

Legal and Compliance Interaction
- Legal must be looped in before any redaction or cross-border evidence transfer.
- If the investigation crosses EU/UK data subject claims, obtain a formal Legal Directive before decrypting EU-resident artifacts for non-EU reviewers.

Escalation and Risk Exceptions
- If required decrypt keys are unavailable because of key compromise or HSM failure, escalate to Head of Security and Legal immediately; document the exception and preserve sealed key-wrapping evidence.
- For high-risk incidents that require immediate action (e.g., active exfiltration), follow the Emergency Containment Checklist and note deviations in the evidence manifest.

Operational Notes and Common Pitfalls
- Do not rely on a single audit stream; always correlate at least two independent sources (gateway + auth-service) to avoid single-point-of-failure in timeline reconstruction.
- Watch for clock drift on older hosts; include host NTP offsets in metadata.
- When packaging large volumes (>50GB), compress per-residency shards separately and include decompression instructions.

Example Audit Event (sanitized)
```
{
  "event_id": "e3b0c442-...",
  "service": "gateway",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-09T18:12:23.123Z",
  "trace_id": "4f8b2c1a-...",
  "user_id": "svc-analytics@redwood",
  "action": "model.invoke",
  "resource": "model:embed-11b:eu/shard-17",
  "auth_decision": "GRANTED",
  "policy_version": "pol-v3.14",
  "residency": "eu",
  "monotonic_sequence": 120345678
}
```

Post-Incident Review and Lessons Learned
- Every playback should produce a short After Action Note (AAN) including: what was reconstructed, confidence levels, missing artifacts, time to package, and suggested process/tooling improvements.
- Maintain a quarterly review of evidence playbacks to ensure the runbook keeps up with changes in feature-flagging, model-routing, and retention automation.

Appendix A: Tooling and Permissions Matrix
- redwood-audit-cli: extraction (role: audit-extractor)
- redwood-keys: signing (role: evidence-signer)
- evidence-store: long-term storage (role: evidence-custodian)
- configctl / kubectl: config snapshots (role: infra-read)
- HSM console: wrap/unwrap (role: hsm-ops)

Appendix B: Evidence Retention & Export Rules Summary
- Short-term forensic bundles: retained for 90 days in evidence-store unless legal hold extends.
- Legal hold: evidence may be sequestered indefinitely via Legal order; Security will mark packages as sealed.
- Cross-border export: follow residency labels — EU-residency artifacts cannot be exported outside EU evidence vault without Legal Authority.

Contact and Escalation
- Security Oncall: pager +1-555-0100 (internal)
- Evidence Custodian rotation: security-evidence@redwood.com
- Legal intake: legal-intake@redwood.com
